title: Demand Service Rate Programs: When a Response Guarantee Is Missed
content:
*A caller says the technician arrived too late. When is a credit owed at all?*

Where a technician reaches the building later than the guarantee the call's classification carries, the
customer is credited. The guarantee is met when the technician is on site no later than the response
hours of that classification counted in elapsed hours from the moment the call was accepted, counting
whole and part hours alike and running through nights, weekends and holidays without pause.

*And how much is that credit?*

The clause that answered that question is no longer in force:

> The credit is the tier's credit rate applied to the labor charge of that call, capped at the tier's ceiling for one missed response, and it is applied to the invoice the call was billed on.

*Are there calls where nothing is owed although the technician was late?*

Yes. No credit is due where the building denied access, where the caller was not reachable to let the
technician in, or where the call was held because the account stood over its credit limit.

*What about a program that carries no credit rate?*

A tier whose credit rate is zero owes no credit at all, and the correct answer to such a caller is that
the tier carries no response guarantee, not a goodwill payment. Under the Demand Service Rate Programs
that is the Time & Material Account, whose credit rate and ceiling both stand at 0.

*Where does the clock start and stop?*

It starts at the moment the call was accepted and stops at the moment the technician is on site. It runs
through nights, weekends and holidays without pause, and part hours count as much as whole ones. On a
classification carrying a guarantee of 12 elapsed hours, a call accepted at two in the afternoon is met
by an arrival at two in the morning the following day, that being exactly 12 elapsed hours later, and
missed by an arrival at half past two that morning.
